fact: NIRA says all CRVS registration systems are under one authority and the NIN is issued automatically once a birth notification is made; it also says push and pull between NSIS and the marriage system is still lacking and death registration is very disconnected.
NIRA runs both birth registration (issuing birth certificates) and the National Identification Numbers, one body handling both, according to its registrar Claire Ollama.

Nile Post reports that NIRA's mandate covers registration and identification of citizens and resident foreigners as well as civil registration of births, deaths, adoptions, guardianship orders and marriages, so one body holds both.
Under the Registration of Persons Act 2015 as amended in 2024, NIRA holds the National Identification Register and also handles births, deaths and, since 2024, marriage registration.

The Uganda Registration Services Bureau says the Directorate of Civil Registration moved from URSB to the National Identification Registration Authority (NIRA) from 1 October 2024, putting civil registration and national identification under one body.

The Parliament of Uganda committee report on the Registration of Persons (Amendment) Bill 2024 backs moving civil registration functions (marriage) from URSB to NIRA so that registration of persons from birth, identification, marriage and death sits under one agency, following a 2021 Cabinet decision.

Bill No. 39 of 27 March 2024, from the Minister for Internal Affairs, would amend the Registration of Persons Act 2015 to transfer administration of the civil registration laws (Children Act, marriage Acts) to the National Identification and Registration Authority, so that civil registration sits in that one agency.
